premises.text: When status reports travel only by email, companies make worse decisions, duplicate work, and lose money because information stays private
premises.evidence_span: decisions are less informed, work is duplicated, and ultimately, companies lose money because of this

premises.text: Managers launch reporting by specifying employees, schedule, and template content in about thirty seconds
premises.evidence_span: 30 seconds, and her life is already easier

premises.text: ThinkFuse makes reports more consistent and timely, shares them with the team, and reminds writers so managers are not the harassing party
premises.evidence_span: the managers don't have to be the bad guy harassing people to write reports, because ThinkFuse does that for them

premises.text: Status reports are a shareable communication class that can map changing people-project relationships across the firm—the business graph
premises.evidence_span: status reports are really designed to be shared. And when you look at them across an entire company, you can start to map the relationships between people and projects

premises.text: Users can search people and reports to find specialists, client relationships, and who is in a given office
premises.evidence_span: by looking across the recently submitted status reports, she can see which of them is working with Acme

premises.text: Project follow and centralized recipient lists replace error-prone weekly email copy-paste distribution
premises.evidence_span: before, Sarah would have to manually copy and paste a long list of email addresses week after week

value.text: Shared understanding that aligns people and resources through accessible, consistent status reports
value.evidence_span: more powerful to align people and resources across an organization

causal_links.evidence_span: how ThinkFuse helps you leverage that information
making status reports more accessible, by making them more consistent
each person understanding the entire puzzle and where their pieces fit in
